title: Distinguishing Weyl rank and central parameters
statement: Can \(R_{n,k}\) or \(D_{n,k}\), over a fixed characteristic-zero field, be isomorphic for different pairs \((n,k)\)? The earlier occurrence 1964-38.1 concerns the ring version without additional central parameters; the present occurrence states the stronger division-ring answer.
status: As of 9 November 2026: solved in the negative, exactly as formulated over the fixed base field, by \citet[\S4]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}. This is independent of the fixed-rank Dixmier endomorphism problem. No earlier GP identifier was supplied in the previous index.

title: Universal determinant for a division ring
statement: Determine the universal abelian quotient of \(\mathrm{GL}_{\infty}(D)\) for a division ring \(D\).
status: As of 9 November 2026: already solved before the talk. The Dieudonn\'e determinant identifies this quotient with \(D^{\times}_{\mathrm{ab}}\) \citep{dieudonne1943determinants}.

title: Automorphisms of Weyl division rings
statement: Determine \(\operatorname{Aut}_{L}D_{n,k}\). The developed subproblem fixes \(L=\mathbb C\), \(n=1\), \(k=0\), and a rational subfield \(\mathbb C(x)\).
status: As of 9 November 2026: partial, with no full classification found in the documented searches. The rational-subfield stabilizer is known \citep{alevdumas1998invariants}; polynomial automorphism classifications and results on finite-group invariant fields \citep{makarlimanov1984automorphisms,schwarz2024generalizations} do not determine the full group. This chapter proves the restricted normal form, finite-group splitting, and an exact criterion for which rational translations are inner; no novelty claim is attached to these elementary consequences.
